tours.name: Vimy Ridge & Somme Canadian Battlefield Tour
intro: Experience two of the most important battlefields in Canadian military history in a single day. Departing from Arras, travel south to the Somme and walk the preserved battlefield at Beaumont-Hamel before following the Canadian Corps to Courcelette and the graves of ADANAC Military Cemetery.

After lunch in the Somme countryside, return north through Mont-Saint-Éloi to Vimy Ridge, where all four divisions of the Canadian Corps fought together in April 1917. Walk the preserved battlefield, stand beneath the Canadian National Vimy Memorial and finish at Cabaret-Rouge British Cemetery, the resting place from which Canada’s Unknown Soldier was selected.

tours.name: Ypres & Passchendaele Canadian Battlefield Tour
intro: Travel from Arras into the heart of Canada’s First World War story, beginning with the preserved frontline trenches at Vimy Ridge and the Canadian battlefield at Hill 70 before continuing north toward Belgium and the Ypres Salient. Along the way, visit a sector associated with the famous Christmas Truce of 1914 and follow the evolution of the Western Front from the early trench battles to the great offensives of 1917.

In Flanders, stand at Essex Farm, forever associated with Canadian doctor John McCrae and his poem “In Flanders Fields,” before exploring the Battle of Passchendaele through the Memorial Museum Passchendaele 1917, Tyne Cot Cemetery and Crest Farm Canadian Memorial. This small-group tour combines preserved trenches, battlefield landscapes and personal stories at some of the most important Canadian sites of the Great War.

tours.name: Western Front & Normandy: 5-Day Tour
intro: Journey across two world wars during an unforgettable five-day battlefield tour through France and Belgium.

Beginning in the historic city of Arras, the first two days follow the Canadians across the Western Front. Explore the preserved trenches and tunnels of Vimy Ridge, visit the battlefields of Hill 70 and Canada's Hundred Days, and travel into Belgium to walk the ground at Ypres and Passchendaele. The Western Front portion concludes beneath the Menin Gate with the moving nightly Last Post Ceremony.

The journey then continues through Normandy to Bayeux. Cross Pegasus Bridge, follow the American airborne divisions through the fields and villages behind Utah Beach, and explore Pointe du Hoc, Omaha Beach and the Normandy American Cemetery.

Combining Canada's most important First World War battlefields with the celebrated D-Day sites of Normandy, this tour is ideal for travellers seeking a comprehensive introduction to the two defining conflicts of the twentieth century.

tours.name: Juno Beach from Paris
intro: Leave Paris behind for an unforgettable journey to the Normandy coast and discover the remarkable story of the brave Canadians who landed at Juno Beach in 1944.

Walk the sands where Canadian soldiers stormed ashore under devastating fire. See the famous Canada House at Bernières-sur-Mer and explore the surviving German defences of Hitler's Atlantic Wall. At the Juno Beach Centre, discover Canada's story and follow an expert Canadian guide into original German bunkers overlooking the landing beach.

After lunch in the seaside town of Courseulles-sur-Mer, continue inland along the route followed by Canadian soldiers on D-Day. Pay your respects at Bény-sur-Mer Canadian War Cemetery, stand at Hell's Corner near the furthest point reached by Canadian troops on June 6, and visit the historic Abbaye d'Ardenne.

tours.name: Juno Beach from Bayeux
intro: Stand on Juno Beach, where brave Canadians famously broke Hitler's Atlantic Wall under intense fire on D-Day. Explore the surviving German coastal defences and visit the Juno Beach Centre, Canada's main memorial and museum in Normandy.

Your journey continues beyond the beaches, tracing the Canadian advance through the villages and fields outside the historic city of Caen. Visit the battlefield of Authie, the Waffen SS headquarters at Abbaye d'Ardenne, Carpiquet and Hill 67, where Canadian soldiers faced some of the most determined German resistance of the Normandy campaign.
Along the way, visit both iconic landmarks and lesser-known battlefield locations that reveal the courage, sacrifice and achievements of the Canadians who liberated France in the summer of 1944.

tours.name: The Complete Normandy Experience: 3-Day Tour
intro: Discover the remarkable history and beauty of Normandy during a three-day journey based in the medieval town of Bayeux.

The first two days explore the principal American, British and Canadian battlefields of D-Day. Follow the airborne landings behind Utah Beach, stand on the sands of Omaha, walk among the surviving German guns at Longues-sur-Mer and discover the stories of Gold Beach, Juno Beach and Pegasus Bridge.
On the third day, travel beyond the battlefields to Mont-Saint-Michel, one of France's most spectacular historic landmarks, and explore the medieval island village and its ancient abbey.

tours.name: The Normandy Explorer: 5-Day Tour
intro: Discover the remarkable history, culture and scenery of Normandy during a five-day journey based in the historic city of Caen.

From the airborne landing grounds and invasion beaches of D-Day to the medieval splendour of Mont-Saint-Michel, this tour explores the many stories that have shaped Normandy. Follow the American paratroopers through the fields around Sainte-Mère-Église, stand on the sands of Omaha, explore the British and Canadian landing sectors and visit the site of the daring assault on Pegasus Bridge.

Beyond the battlefields, travel through the picturesque villages of the Pays d'Auge, sample the flavours of Normandy along the Route du Cidre and discover the historic towns of Lisieux, Cabourg and Bayeux.

tours.name: The Dieppe Raid
intro: On 19 August 1942, more than 6,000 Allied troops, most of them Canadian, landed along the coast of occupied France during the Dieppe Raid. Within hours, the operation had ended in disaster, leaving thousands killed, wounded or captured.

Beginning in Dieppe, this full-day battlefield tour follows the Canadians from the beaches where they came ashore to the surrounding cliffs, villages and fortified positions that shaped the battle. Stand on Blue Beach at Puys, explore the battlefield at Pourville and discover surviving Atlantic Wall defences hidden among the picturesque white cliffs of the Normandy coast.
The day concludes at Dieppe Canadian War Cemetery, where many of those who fell during the raid remain buried.

Although historians continue to debate its legacy, the Dieppe Raid exposed serious weaknesses in Allied amphibious planning. Many of its lessons influenced preparations for the Normandy landings and the successful Canadian assault on Juno Beach less than two years later.
